questions.q: What two ingredients define the general CSS construction?
options: One classical code used twice with no additional requirement
Two unrelated random binary matrices with no structural condition between them
A pair of classical linear codes C1 and C2, satisfying the nesting condition C2-dual is a subset of C1
A single classical code and a single quantum ancilla qubit
questions.explain: The CSS construction requires two classical codes C1 and C2 with C2's dual nested inside C1 -- this nesting is what guarantees valid, commuting quantum stabilizers.

questions.q: In the CSS construction, where do the X-type and Z-type stabilizers come from?
options: X-type stabilizers come from C1's structure, Z-type stabilizers come from C2's structure
X-type stabilizers come from ancilla qubits, unrelated to either classical code
Z-type stabilizers are generated randomly, independent of C1 or C2
Both X-type and Z-type stabilizers always come from the same single classical code with no distinction
questions.explain: The CSS recipe explicitly assigns X-type stabilizers from C1's parity-check structure and Z-type stabilizers from C2's, which is why the nesting condition between the two codes matters.

questions.q: Why is the Steane code described as the 'self-dual special case' of the CSS construction?
options: Because 'self-dual' means the code has zero stabilizer generators
Because the Steane code uses no classical code at all
Because C1 = C2 = the Hamming(7,4) code, and the nesting condition reduces to the self-orthogonality verified in the previous lesson
Because the Steane code requires two completely different, unrelated classical codes
questions.explain: When C1 and C2 are literally the same classical code, the general nesting condition C2-dual subset of C1 becomes the self-orthogonality condition verified directly on the Hamming(7,4) matrix in the Steane code lesson.

questions.q: Why do CSS codes reuse classical coding theory, as opposed to needing entirely new quantum-specific design methods?
options: Because CSS codes abandon the stabilizer formalism entirely
Because quantum errors are identical to classical bit errors with no distinction
Because CSS codes don't actually involve any classical coding theory at all
Because X errors and Z errors are each handled by one of the two classical codes, so decades of classical coding-theory results (distance, decoding, performance) apply directly to each half
questions.explain: The CSS trick of handling X errors via C1 and Z errors via C2 lets each half of the problem be analyzed using well-established classical coding theory, rather than inventing new machinery from scratch.

questions.q: What other code in this course, covered in the next chapter, is also built using the CSS structure?
options: The classical repetition code from chapter 2
Only the Shor 9-qubit code uses CSS, not the surface code
The surface code, whose X-type plaquette stabilizers and Z-type vertex stabilizers follow the same CSS pairing on a 2D lattice
No other code in this course uses the CSS structure
questions.explain: The surface code (chapter 5) is also a CSS code, pairing X-type and Z-type stabilizers on a 2D lattice instead of a 7-qubit block -- the same underlying principle in a different, hardware-friendly geometry.
